{{Quote|All we have are a few guesses — and some secondhand sources that are little better than legends. The grimoiries of the Gree Enclave say the work of the Ancient Masters — the Celestials — was undone by two curses unleashed by the Soul Hunters, whom we identify as the Rakata. The Gree name those curses the Gray Swallowing and the Faceless Mouths, and further refer to them as the Hollowers of Beings and the Eaters of Worlds.|Dr. Insmot Bowen discusses the Rakatan revolt with Bevel Lemelisk and Conan Antonio Motti|<ref name="The Celestials" />}}
The '''Rakatan revolt''' was an uprising of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Species/Legends|species]] against the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] that occurred millennia before the birth of the [[Old Republic era|Old Republic]] whose inception and outcome have been lost in time.

==Prelude==
[[File:Rakata_First_Contact.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Kwa uplifted the Rakata from their primitive state, teaching them the ways of the Force on Lehon.]]
The origins of the Rakatan revolt dated back to the dawn of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Species/Legends|species]]' civilization on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]], a terrestrial world located in the [[Tempered Wastes]] of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].<ref name="The Celestials" /><ref name="TEA" /> Many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before [[36,453 BBY]],<ref name="DOTJ Date">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 4|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 4]] indicates that the battle between the Kwa and the Rakata occurred prior to the [[Tho Yor Arrival]], which [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi 0|''Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi'' 0]] places in [[36,453 BBY]].</ref> the [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]]&mdash;a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] species from the planet [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]&mdash;uplifted the Rakata civilization, who were taught the power of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and were given advanced technology.<ref name="DOTJ 4" /> During these times the Rakata became the client species of the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]], who were the dominant galactic power and Kwa's own beneficiaries.<ref name="The Celestials" />

Following the devastating [[Battle between the Kwa and the Rakata|conflict with the Kwa]], the Rakata promptly developed<ref name="DOTJ 4" /> the [[Force-drive|first known hyperdrive]],<ref name="GH05">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 05: Rise of the Infinite Empire}}</ref> discovering that they could use the energy of Force-sensitive slaves among the populations they conquered to fuel their warships. Thus the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] was born, which expanded with each new conquest and discovery of another planet rich in the Force.<ref name="DOTJ 4" />

==The revolt==
{{Quote|They disappeared. We don't know what happened to them. They may have been trapped inside our galaxy by their barrier and destroyed by the Rakatan revolt. They may have escaped through the barrier. Or perhaps they withdrew into some dimension beyond the reach of the Rakata and ourselves.|Dr. Insmot Bowen discusses the Celestials with Bevel Lemelisk and Conan Antonio Motti|<ref name="The Celestials" />}}
Speculation holds that the Celestials had crafted the [[western barrier]] that bisected [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] west of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]<ref name="The Celestials" /> with the help of their servants, the [[Gree (species)/Legends|Gree]], the Kwa, and the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]]<ref name="EGtW" /> in order to contain the upstart Rakata.<ref name="TEA" /> However, the newly-formed Infinite Empire had spread out over the Unknown Regions and conquered much of the eastern galaxy around [[35,000 BBY]].<ref name="NEGtAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> Sometime prior to [[33,598 BBY]],<ref name="KotOR Date">In ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'', the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] interface of the [[Builder Forge]] asserts that the computer was last accessed by the [[Rakata/Legends|Builders]] 29,642 standard years before [[3956 BBY]].</ref> the Rakata had captured the forest world of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], and installed a [[Builder Forge|terraforming computer]] on the planet to manipulate Kashyyyk's [[Wroshyr tree/Legends|wroshyr trees]].<ref name="KotOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

The ancient grimoires of the [[Gree Enclave/Legends|Gree Enclave]], which referred to the Celestials as the "Ancient Masters," recorded that their work was undone by curses unleashed by the Rakata, or the "Soul Hunters," which they called the "Gray Swallowing" and the "Hollowers of Beings," and further referred to them as the "Faceless Mouths" and "Eaters of Worlds." At some point more than 30,000 years before [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], the Celestials disappeared from the galaxy.<ref name="The Celestials" /> By [[30,000 BBY]], the Celestials were nowhere to be found.<ref name="TUR" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|But the evidence is considerably more clear that the Rakata waged devastating war against the Kwa and the Gree. And the Killiks simply vanished. All three, we believe, were key client species of the Celestials. It looks as if the Rakata were determined to exterminate or drive out their rivals among the Celestial slave species.|Dr. Insmot Bowen discusses the war against the Celestial client species with Bevel Lemelisk and Conan Antonio Motti|<ref name="The Celestials" />}}
By 30,000 BBY, the Celestials were nowhere to be found,<ref name="TUR" /> and therefore ceased to pose a threat to the expanding Infinite Empire.<ref name="TEA" /> The Rakatan Infinite Empire had taken center stage as a dominant galactic power stretching from the Tempered Wastes to the furthest reaches of the eastern galaxy,<ref name="TEA" /> linking over five hundred Force-rich worlds.<ref name="GH05" /> The Rakata turned their attention to the [[War against Celestial client species|subjugation]] of their major rivals<ref name="TEA" /> among the Celestial client species,<ref name="The Celestials" /> namely the Killiks,<ref name="EGtW" /> the Gree Empire and the [[Kwa holdings]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Gree were [[Defeat of the Gree Empire|driven]] back to their home cluster, while the Kwa were [[Annexation of Kwa holdings|all but exterminated]] by the Infinite Empire.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Infinite_Empire_JMGD.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The victory in the Rakatan revolt brought about an era of stability to the Infinite Empire that persisted until the Rakata Civil War.]]
Similarly, the Killiks vanished from the galaxy and [[Great Migration|migrated]] beyond the veil of the Unknown Regions, which was an act presumed to be attributed to the Celestials.<ref name="TEA" /> After the construction of [[Centerpoint Station]], it was claimed by the Killiks that the Celestials had grown angry with their Kind and had emptied them from their homeworld of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="DN:TJK">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref> It was theorized that the Celestials drove the Killiks into the Unknown Regions after they devoured their own homeworld and attempted to lay claim to another planet.<ref name="DN:TSW">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref> The Mnggal-Mnggal similarly claimed that it had witnessed the sudden withdrawal of the Celestials from the galaxy in this era.<ref name="TUR" />

The eventual fate of the Celestials was unclear to later [[Historian/Legends|historians]]. Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]] posited that they may have been trapped inside the galaxy by their barrier and destroyed by the Rakatan revolt, or they may have escaped through the barrier. He also suggested that they may have withdrawn from this dimension completely.<ref name="The Celestials" /> Others, like the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] mused on the possibility that the Celestials were the ones who, according to Jedi and Sith legend, merged into the Force to control its path.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

==Legacy==
{{Quote|When our ancestors were still howling primates, our galaxy was ruled by a species that could create, reconfigure or destroy star systems according to some unimaginable whim. At some point more than 30,000 years ago, the Celestials' dominion vanished. Yet there's no record that they were ever conquered. We don't even know what they looked like. We never saw the body — they simply disappeared. Considering what they could do eons ago, gentlemen, ask yourself this: ''What if they return''?|Dr. Insmot Bowen on the possibility of Celestials returning to the galaxy|<ref name="The Celestials" />}}
In the year 1 BBY, Dr. Insmot Bowen, a specialist in [[Pre-Republic era|pre-Republic]] history at the [[Obroan Institute for Archaeology]], gave a debriefing to [[General/Legends|General]] [[Arhul Kurumenga]] of the [[Imperial Department of Military Research/Legends|Imperial Department of Military Research]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], and [[Master of Imperial Projects]] [[Bevel Lemelisk]] relating to various discoveries that would provide hints, albeit minimal, regarding aspects of the Celestials, including their conflict with and eventual defeat at the hands of the Rakata.<ref name="The Celestials" />

Motti doubted the historicity of the Rakata and Celestial species in general, going so far as to dismiss the stories about them as little more than "arrant nonsense" fit only to be the subject of "[[holothriller]]s." However, the aforementioned Dr. Bowen, believed the stories of the Celestial species and the war in which they fought, going so far as to suggest that the Celestials might still be out in the universe in one form or another, a potential threat to the stability of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]].<ref name="The Celestials" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Rakatan revolt was supposed to have been mentioned in ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' but was cut by [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="tumblr">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/20843004826/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-1|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 1}}</ref> It was eventually unveiled in the [[Star Wars Blog]] article [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut — The Celestials]].<ref name="The Celestials" />
